subject: Streaming/chat latency incident — mitigation & postmortem timeline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@fintecture.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Streaming/chat latency — immediate mitigations & ask

Alex —

Thanks for flagging the degraded streaming performance you observed this morning. I’m very sorry for the disruption — we know low-latency streaming is critical for your chat UX. Quick updates and actionable steps you can take now: 

- What we observed: a spike in end-to-end token latency for streaming responses that affected long-lived chat sessions (clients with open streaming SSE/WS connections).
- Immediate mitigations we’ve applied: we pushed a routing config to shift new streaming traffic to a warm pool of nodes and temporarily increased streaming autoscaling thresholds for your account.
- Client-side short-term options (if you can make a change):
  - Switch to non-streaming (polled) responses for heavy concurrent flows while we stabilize streaming. This reduces latency variance.
  - Reduce the streaming token batch size (token_window) to 8–16 tokens if your client supports it.
  - Fall back from SSE to short-poll every 1–2s for critical user flows as a stopgap.

I’ve attached a short mitigation checklist (mitigation_steps.md) and a tiny logs snapshot (logs_snippet.txt) showing the error patterns we correlated. If you can confirm whether your client can accept a non-streaming fallback or token_window change, we’ll coordinate a targeted rollback to the faster path for your traffic.

We’ll keep you updated as we complete the postmortem and root-cause analysis. Again — apologies and thank you for patience.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation_steps.md (text)
Attachment: logs_snippet.txt (text)

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-09T08:33:00Z
Subject: RE: Streaming/chat latency — immediate mitigations & ask (internal notes)

Quick internal summary:
- Root cause (initial): regression in a batching heuristic in the serving runtime that caused excessive coalescing for streaming sessions with large KV caches; under certain workload patterns this increased tail latency significantly.
- What we did: rolled a config that lowers the coalescing window for streaming endpoints for affected model families and enabled a short-lived autoscale bump for accounts with sustained streaming concurrency.
- Open action items:
  1) Infra: confirm the coalescing-window rollback holds for 4 hours — @vivek please confirm metrics look stable.
  2) Platform: add a quick client-side mitigation guide we can send to customers (Marissa can use).
  3) Eng: collect full perf traces and one hour worth of combined lanes for postmortem (INC-7742).

We should also offer a short private postmortem review with Fintecture if they want — recommend next-day slot.

-Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Note: forwarding logs to SRE on-call and creating ticket INC-7742.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@fintecture.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-09T12:06:00Z
Subject: RE: Streaming/chat latency — immediate mitigations & ask

Alex — quick update: we rolled the targeted config change at 11:00 UTC and have seen median streaming latency return to expected ranges for your routed sessions. A few notes: 

- We kept the streaming autoscale bump in place for your account for two hours to absorb the backlog while nodes warmed.
- If you prefer, we can patch your routing rule so new streams default to a lower-latency model variant (lower context/window) for the next 24 hours; this is reversible.
- We’ll follow up with a postmortem and a proposed permanent fix timeline (ETA 48–72 hours for a non-disruptive kernel-level patch, 7–10 days for a full code-level release).

Next steps for your team (recommended):
1) If you can tolerate short polling for the next 6–12 hours for non-critical conversations, that will minimize user impact while we validate stability.
2) Confirm whether you want us to enable the temporary routing to the lower-context variant for the next 24 hours (yes/no).

I’m available for a 30-minute call this afternoon if you want to walk through the checklist together.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: incident_report.pdf (summary stub)
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-09-streaming-latency

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@fintecture.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@fintecture.com
Date: 2026-03-09T14:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Streaming/chat latency — immediate mitigations & ask

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the fast action. Quick Q: will any of the troubleshooting steps or logs you pulled include customer data (message text/user IDs)? Our security team asked about scope of data pulled.

Also, please go ahead and enable the lower-context variant for 24h for our production route. We’ll plan to roll the short-poll fallback for non-critical flows if you still see noise later tonight.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, Fintecture

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-10T17:42:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: streaming/chat latency postmortem offer and next steps

Alex —

Thanks again for the quick coordination yesterday. We’ve completed the initial data collection and a short internal RCA: the serving runtime coalescing heuristic was too aggressive for a specific token-size distribution seen in your workload, which increased tail latency for streaming sessions with large KV caches. The engineering team has a non-disruptive patch that reduces the coalescing window (deployed to canary at 09:00 UTC) and a full fix scheduled for Saturday (2026-03-14).

What you can expect now:
- Stability: the canary has been stable for 24 hours in your region; we see restored tail-latency percentiles in the affected routes.
- Transparency: we will publish a written postmortem by 2026-03-12 (internal draft attached) and are happy to run a private postmortem review with your engineers.
- Remediation credit: because this impacted production SLA for a customer route, I’ve initiated a goodwill credit request (ticket INC-7742). We’ll notify you when the credit is approved.

If you’d like a 30–45 minute postmortem walkthrough, I can propose two slots: Friday 09:00–09:45 UTC or Monday 16:00–16:45 UTC. Please let me know which works for your team.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_report.pdf (draft)
